method: Fixed logical CPU, rotated lanes, wall and process CPU time, exact node counts; unrelated processes were not interrupted.

caveats: Perft/FEN/SAN EPD sources include 4-field EPD notation, converted to 6-field FEN before invoking the standard-only competitor.
Drumevp perft explicitly SKIPS Zobrist maintenance. Both no-hash and full-hash (diagnostic upstream make) perft timings are included; GigaChess uses its public Board.perft.

Chess.js suppresses phantom EP targets in serialized FEN, while drumevp may preserve them after a double pawn push. FEN board/turn/castling/clocks are checked separately; EP presentation differences are counted and legal en-passant moves are checked independently.
Drumevp has 32-bit packed moves, standard chess only, no comparable SAN/PGN or Chess960 API; report N/A, not a win.
Drumevp cached move list is a cache lookup, not a new legal-move generation; comparison deliberately separate.
Cross-library perft counts prove aggregate node parity, NOT equal per-position legal moves or input validation.
Warm-up excludes 2 preliminary passes; 7 (or --runs N) samples rotate engine order and report medians/p10/p90. Shared-server contention can affect results; repeat independently for significance.

Move list generation is not API-identical: chess.js emits SAN, chessops provides destination bitsets (promotions unexpanded), GigaChess/drumevp return packed moves. Never treat those four numbers as a pure movegen microbenchmark.
